_This page is generated from src/checks/, so it says what the tool does._

A check is one object in the `checks` list of a `case.json`. Every check has a `type`, and takes an optional `weight`, a positive number that defaults to 1. [Write a case](../guides/write-a-case.md) shows how to use them.

## Check types

| Check                 | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Scores 1 when                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `skill_loaded`        | optional `skill`, optional `anyOf`, optional `first`, optional `ignoring`, optional `via`, optional `resolved`, optional `by`. A load is a real one: a skill-kind call that names the skill, or a read-kind or `cat`-style shell call of `SKILL.md` in the loaded subject's own copy of the skill. A `grep`, a listing, and a path in the workspace that merely looks like `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` are not loads. With `first: true` the first skill load must be a named skill, and no tool call that does not fit `ignoring` may come before it; every call of the run counts, a subagent's included, unless `by` limits both the loads and the calls to one agent. It takes exactly one of `skill` and `anyOf`, and `ignoring` only with `first`. Under `--lenient`, a check with neither `via` nor `resolved` keeps the 0.0.1 rule for one release: any tool input that mentions `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, in any case. | The agent loaded that skill, or any of the skills in `anyOf`, through the skill tool, a read of its `SKILL.md`, or a shell command that reads it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `skill_not_loaded`    | `skill`, optional `via`, optional `resolved`, optional `by`. It counts loads as `skill_loaded` does, including `via`, `resolved` and `by`, and keeps the 0.0.1 rule under `--lenient` in the same way.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The agent did not load that skill.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `skill_available`     | `skill`. It reads the skills the harness reported at startup, so it needs the capability `skillListing`; a harness without it makes the case not applicable, and a run whose harness reported no skills scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The harness listed that skill among the skills it loaded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `skill_not_available` | `skill`. It reads the skills the harness reported at startup, so it needs the capability `skillListing`; a harness without it makes the case not applicable, and a run whose harness reported no skills scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The harness did not list that skill among the skills it loaded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `skill_file_read`     | `skill`, `path`, optional `via`. Reads count through a read-kind call or a `cat`-style shell command, as for `skill_loaded`; `path` is relative to the skill's directory, not to the workspace, and may be a glob such as `references/*.md`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | The agent read a file of that skill's directory other than `SKILL.md`, whose path relative to the directory matches the glob `path`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `output_matches`      | `pattern`, optional `flags`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The final answer matches the regular expression.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `output_lacks`        | `pattern`, optional `flags`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | The final answer does not match the regular expression.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `output_contains`     | `text`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The final answer contains that text.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `output_not_contains` | `text`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The final answer does not contain that text.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `file_exists`         | `path`, optional `created`, optional `root`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | A file exists at `path` and can be read; with `created`, one that the root did not hold before the run. A glob needs one matching file. A directory is not a file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `file_matches`        | `path`, `pattern`, optional `flags`, optional `quantifier`, optional `root`. A file is read as UTF-8, with replacement characters for bytes that are not, and a file over 5 MB scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | A file at `path` matches the regular expression. With a glob, one matching file is enough unless `quantifier` is `all`. No match for the path scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `file_lacks`          | `path`, `pattern`, optional `flags`, optional `quantifier`, optional `root`. A file over 5 MB, or one that cannot be read, and a directory that cannot be listed, cannot be shown to lack the pattern, so each scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | No file at `path` matches the regular expression. With a glob, every matching file must lack it unless `quantifier` is `any`. A path that matches no file scores 1. A plain path that names a directory, or ends in `/`, means every file under it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `file_lines`          | `path`, at least one of `min`, `max`, optional `root`. A file over 5 MB scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Every file at `path` has from `min` to `max` lines. A path that matches no file scores 0. A plain path that names a directory, or ends in `/`, means every file under it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `file_absent`         | `path`, optional `root`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Nothing exists at `path`, whether a file, a directory or a link. A path that matches nothing scores 1, and so does one that leads nowhere: a dangling link, or a link that leaves the root. A directory that cannot be listed scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `file_unchanged`      | `path`, optional `root`. A plain path that names a directory, or ends in `/`, covers every file under it. A mode-only change is not a change, and a link is matched by its own path, never followed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | No file at `path` was created, modified or deleted by the run. A path that matches no file in the seed and none now scores 1. A directory that could not be listed, and could hold a match, scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `file_changed`        | `path`, optional `root`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | A file at `path` was created, modified or deleted by the run. A path that matches no file scores 0, and the reason names a directory that could not be listed and could have held one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `files_changed_only`  | `allow`, optional `ignore`, optional `root`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Every path the run created, modified or deleted, except the ones `ignore` names, matches a path or glob of `allow`. A plain directory path covers everything under it. A directory that could not be listed scores 0, unless an `allow` or `ignore` path covers all of it.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `file_count`          | `path`, optional `min`, optional `max`, optional `root`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The number of files that `path` matches is from `min` (default 1) to `max`. Directories are not counted. A plain path that names a directory, or ends in `/`, means every file under it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `dir_exists`          | `path`, optional `root`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | A directory exists at `path`. A file or a link to one does not count.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `tool_called`         | at least one of `kind`, `name`, `by`, optional `inputMatches`, optional `flags`, optional `inputLinesMax`, optional `inputLinesMin`, optional `minDurationMs`, optional `maxDurationMs`, optional `min`, optional `max`, optional `sameTurn`, optional `first`. A count sees every call of the run, a subagent's included, unless `by` names the agent. With `by` alone (no `kind` or `name`) it counts every call of that agent, so `{ by: { agent: "research-planner" }, max: 0 }` says the planner made no tool call; `min` then defaults to 0 when `max` is 0. With `first` and `by`, the first call that agent made must fit, and with no `by` the run's first call. `sameTurn` needs a harness with `turnGrouping`; elsewhere the case is not applicable. `by` needs `childCalls`.                                                                                                                                     | The agent made tool calls that fit every given field, and their number is from `min` to `max`. With `sameTurn`, they were all issued in one assistant turn.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `tool_not_called`     | at least one of `kind`, `name`, `by`, optional `inputMatches`, optional `flags`, optional `inputLinesMax`, optional `inputLinesMin`, optional `minDurationMs`, optional `maxDurationMs`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The agent made no tool call that fits every given field.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `first_tool`          | `matches`, optional `ignoring`. A subagent's calls are in the list too, unless `matches` or an `ignoring` matcher says `by`: `matches` with `by: "main"` fails when a subagent's call comes first.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | The first tool call, once the calls that fit `ignoring` are dropped, fits `matches`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `tool_order`          | optional `before`, optional `after`, optional `sequence`, optional `strict`. It takes exactly one of the pair `before` and `after`, and `sequence`. With `strict: true` a sequence also forbids a later matcher's call before an earlier matcher's first match, and an earlier matcher's call after a later matcher's first match: `[researcher, synthesizer]` allows two researchers, then the synthesizer, and no researcher after it. The check sees every call of the run, a subagent's included, unless a matcher says `by`: `before: { kind: "read", by: { agent: "delegate" } }` is the delegate's read.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The calls come in the order given: with `before` and `after`, the chosen `before` call is earlier than the chosen `after` call; with `sequence`, the matchers match calls in that order.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `transcript_matches`  | `pattern`, optional `flags`, optional `where`, optional `scope`, optional `by`. A pattern sees at most the first 1,000,000 characters of each event. `first_message` is the main agent's first non-empty text, which in a kit whose first action is a tool call is not the text before the first tool call. With `by`, only the events of those agents are tested, and `first_message` and `final_message` are those agents' first and last non-empty text: `by: { "agent": "researcher" }` with `first_message` is the researcher's first line. With a `by` that no event of the chosen `where` fits, `transcript_lacks` scores 0 and not 1, as when the run has no such events at all. `by` needs `childText`.                                                                                                                                                                                                             | At least one of the tested texts matches the regular expression: the assistant's text by default, or the tool inputs, tool outputs or all of them with `where`, in the events that `scope` names.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `transcript_lacks`    | `pattern`, optional `flags`, optional `where`, optional `scope`, optional `by`. A pattern sees at most the first 1,000,000 characters of each event. `first_message` is the main agent's first non-empty text, which in a kit whose first action is a tool call is not the text before the first tool call. With `by`, only the events of those agents are tested, and `first_message` and `final_message` are those agents' first and last non-empty text: `by: { "agent": "researcher" }` with `first_message` is the researcher's first line. With a `by` that no event of the chosen `where` fits, `transcript_lacks` scores 0 and not 1, as when the run has no such events at all. `by` needs `childText`.                                                                                                                                                                                                             | None of the tested texts matches the regular expression. A run with no events of the chosen `where` at all (no assistant text, no tool results or no calls, as `where` says) scores 0, since that usually means the capture is broken. With `tool_output` or `all`, a call in the window with no result also scores 0, as for `tool_output_lacks`. An empty window after a found `before` or `after` cut passes, and a cut whose matcher matches no call scores 0. |
| `tool_output_matches` | `tool`, `pattern`, optional `flags`, optional `which`. The output is the tool's own result, as the stream carried it, never the agent's account of it. A pattern sees at most the first 1,000,000 characters of an output. `flags` belong to `pattern`; the matcher has its own.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | The output of a call that fits `tool` matches the regular expression: any such call, or with `which` the first or the last. A call with no result does not match, and no such call scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `tool_output_lacks`   | `tool`, `pattern`, optional `flags`, optional `which`. Same fields as `tool_output_matches`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | No chosen call's output matches the regular expression. A chosen call with no result cannot be shown to lack the pattern, and no call that fits `tool` scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `tool_output_size`    | `maxBytes`, optional `tool`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | No tool output, or none of the calls that fit `tool`, is over `maxBytes` bytes. A call with no result is ignored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `subject_unchanged`   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | The agent changed nothing in the copy of the subject that the run loaded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `command`             | `run`, optional `expectExit`, optional `stdoutMatches`, optional `stdoutLacks`, optional `flags`, optional `timeoutSeconds`, optional `scoreFrom`. It runs after the agent exits, in the workspace, as you, without a sandbox, and after every other check is scored. See the safety page.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | The command exits with the expected code and its standard output passes. With `scoreFrom: stdout`, the score is the number on the last line of standard output.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `judge`               | `rubric`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Not 0 or 1. A model scores the final answer against the rubric.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `decision`            | `question`, optional `expect`, optional `options`. It takes exactly one of `expect` and `options`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Not 0 or 1. A decision model gives each allowed answer a probability, and the score is the expected value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## Fields

| Field            | Type       | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `skill`          | `text`     | The name of a skill.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `pattern`        | `regex`    | A regular expression.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `text`           | `text`     | Text to look for. The match is exact and case-sensitive.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `kind`           | `kind`     | What the tool does, with the same word in every harness.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `name`           | `regex`    | A regular expression for the harness's own tool name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `inputMatches`   | `regex`    | A regular expression for the tool call's input, written as JSON.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `flags`          | `flags`    | The flags of the check's regular expressions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `inputLinesMax`  | `int`      | The most lines that the call's input may have, counted in its longest string value, found at any depth. A call with no string value has none.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `inputLinesMin`  | `int`      | The fewest lines that the call's input must have, counted in the same way as `inputLinesMax`. `inputLinesMin: 1001` fits a call with a value of more than 1000 lines, so `tool_not_called` with it says that no single write was that long.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `minDurationMs`  | `int`      | The fewest milliseconds that the call took, as its tool result says. A call whose duration is unknown does not fit. Needs a harness with `toolDurations`; elsewhere the case is not applicable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `maxDurationMs`  | `int`      | The most milliseconds that the call took, as its tool result says. A call whose duration is unknown does not fit. Needs a harness with `toolDurations`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `by`             | `by`       | Whose calls, skill loads or text count: `"main"` (the main thread), `"subagent"` (any subagent, at any depth), or `{ "agent": "<name>" }` (agents of that type; a plugin prefix is dropped, so `magic:comment-sicko:comment-sicko` and `comment-sicko` are the same). Absent: every agent. Needs a harness with `childCalls`; on `transcript_matches` and `transcript_lacks`, `childText`.                                                                                                                   |
| `anyOf`          | `texts`    | A list of skill names, any of which is accepted. Give this or `skill`, not both.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `min`            | `count`    | The fewest that pass, a whole number, 0 or more: matching calls for `tool_called`, matching files for `file_count`, lines for `file_lines`. Default: 1 for `tool_called` and `file_count`; 0 for a `tool_called` whose `max` is 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `max`            | `count`    | The most that pass, a whole number, 0 or more: matching calls for `tool_called`, matching files for `file_count`, lines for `file_lines`. Default: no limit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `sameTurn`       | `bool`     | True to require every matching call to be issued in one assistant turn, so that `min` and `max` count calls that were launched together. A matching call with no turn fails it, unless it is the only match. Needs a harness with `turnGrouping`. Default: false.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `first`          | `bool`     | True to require the first thing the agent did to be what the check names: for `tool_called`, the run's first tool call fits the matcher fields, or with `by`, the first call made by that agent does; for `skill_loaded`, the first skill load is the skill, and no tool call outside `ignoring` comes before it. Default: false.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `before`         | `matcher`  | The calls that must come first, as a matcher, with `which` for the first or last of them. Every call counts, a subagent's included, unless the matcher says `by`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `after`          | `matcher`  | The calls that must come second, as a matcher, with `which` for the first or last of them. Every call counts, a subagent's included, unless the matcher says `by`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `sequence`       | `matchers` | A list of matchers that must match calls in this order, with other calls allowed between them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `strict`         | `bool`     | True for a `sequence` to forbid a later matcher's call before an earlier matcher's first match, and an earlier matcher's call after a later matcher's first match. Default: false.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `matches`        | `matcher`  | The matcher that the first tool call must fit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `ignoring`       | `matchers` | Matchers for calls to leave out before looking at the first call, such as a read the agent is allowed to make first.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `via`            | `vias`     | How the skill reached the agent: `"skill_tool"` (a call of the harness's skill tool), `"file_read"` (a read-kind call of a file in the skill's directory), `"shell_read"` (a shell command that `cat`s, `head`s, `tail`s, `less`es, `bat`s, `nl`s or `sed -n`s such a file), or a list of them. `"injected"` is reserved: nothing produces it yet. Default: the three real mechanisms.                                                                                                                       |
| `resolved`       | `bool`     | For `skill_loaded` and `skill_not_loaded`: true counts only a load of a skill of the loaded subject, so a run with no subject that calls the skill tool with a name does not count; false counts only the loads that are not. Default: both count.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `where`          | `enum`     | What the pattern tests: "assistant_text" (the default), "tool_input" (each call's input, written as JSON), "tool_output", or "all" of them. Each event's text is cut to its first 1,000,000 characters first. `tool_output` and `all` need a harness with `toolOutputs`; `assistant_text` needs `assistantText`.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `scope`          | `scope`    | Which events are tested: "any" (the default), "first_message" (the main agent's first non-empty text, wherever it falls), "final_message" (its last non-empty text; with `by`, the first or last text of those agents instead), `{ "before": matcher }` or `{ "after": matcher }` (the events before or after the first call that fits the matcher; no such call scores 0), or `{ "first_message": true, "before": matcher }` (the first text, which scores 0 when it comes after the matcher's first call). |
| `which`          | `enum`     | Which of the calls that fit `tool` count: "first", "last", or "any" of them. Default: "any". A chosen call with no output scores 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `tool`           | `matcher`  | The matcher for the calls whose outputs are tested. For `tool_output_size` it is optional: without it every output counts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `maxBytes`       | `int`      | The most bytes that one tool output may have, as UTF-8 text. A call with no result is ignored.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `path`           | `path`     | A path relative to the root, which may not leave it. The root is the workspace or the home, and for `skill_file_read` the skill's own directory. A path with `*`, `?` or `{` is a glob: `*` and `?` stay within a directory, `**` crosses directories, and `{a,b}` matches either. A glob never follows a link, and a path through a link that leaves the root counts as absent.                                                                                                                             |
| `quantifier`     | `enum`     | For a glob that matches several files: "any" needs one of them to pass, "all" needs every one. Default: "any" for `file_matches`, "all" for `file_lacks`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `root`           | `enum`     | Where the path is looked up: the agent's "workspace", or the run's throwaway "home", for a skill that writes user-level files. Default: "workspace".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `created`        | `bool`     | True to require that the agent created the file: no file at that path was in the root before the run. Default: false.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `allow`          | `texts`    | A non-empty list of globs. Every path the run created, modified or deleted must match one of them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `ignore`         | `texts`    | A list of globs for changed paths to leave out before `allow` is applied, such as a log file the harness writes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `run`            | `text`     | Shell text, run with `/bin/sh -c` in the workspace after the agent exits. It runs as you, without a sandbox.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `expectExit`     | `count`    | The exit code that counts as success. Default: 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `stdoutMatches`  | `regex`    | A regular expression that the command's standard output must match.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `stdoutLacks`    | `regex`    | A regular expression that the command's standard output must not match.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `timeoutSeconds` | `int`      | The seconds the command may take before its process group is killed. The check then scores 0 and the run stays valid. Default: 120.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `scoreFrom`      | `enum`     | How the check scores: "exit" gives 1 or 0, "stdout" reads a number from 0 to 1 on the last non-empty line of standard output, and anything else scores 0. The exit code and the patterns must hold either way. Default: "exit".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `rubric`         | `text`     | Plain text that says what a good answer does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `question`       | `text`     | A question about the final answer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `expect`         | `enum`     | The answer that scores 1 for a yes or no question: "yes" or "no".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `options`        | `answers`  | An object of at least two answers, each with a number from 0 to 1 that says what the answer is worth.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `requires`       | `needs`    | A list of capabilities the check needs, such as `"mcp"`, or `"bin:<name>"` for an executable on the host's `PATH`. A harness that lacks one cannot run the check.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ifUnsupported`  | `enum`     | What a harness that lacks what the check needs does: "skip" drops this check and re-normalizes the weights, "not-applicable" excludes the whole case. Default: "not-applicable".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## Case file keys

The keys of a `case.json`. Any other key is a load error, except a key that starts with `x-` and `$schema`, a string that points an editor at [the schema](config.md#json-schemas).

| Key              | Type        | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checks`         | `object`    | A non-empty list of checks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `weight`         | `number`    | How much the case counts in its suite. Default: 1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `minScore`       | `unit`      | The lowest score the case may get and still pass.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `maxTurns`       | `int`       | The most turns the agent may take. Only Claude Code applies it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `timeoutSeconds` | `int`       | The seconds a run may take. Default: 600.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `requires`       | `needs`     | A list of capabilities the case needs, such as `"mcp"`, or `"bin:<name>"` for an executable on the host's `PATH`. A harness that lacks one reports the case as not applicable.                                                                                                   |
| `harnesses`      | `harnesses` | The harness ids the case is for. Any other harness reports it as not applicable. Needs `note`. A last resort: prefer `requires`.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `note`           | `text`      | Why the case is limited to `harnesses`. The report shows it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `tags`           | `tags`      | Labels for selecting cases with `--tag`, `--tag-all` and `--not-tag`. Each is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `description`    | `text`      | What the case shows, in a sentence.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `targets`        | `texts`     | The names of the skills the case is about. The report counts the cases of each in its coverage table.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `kind`           | `text`      | The kind of case, such as `trigger` or `negative`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `expected`       | `text`      | What a good run does, in a sentence. It is for readers; no check reads it.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `guard`          | `bool`      | True for a case that must keep passing. The report lists it in its own table. Its score counts in the suite score like any other. Default: false.                                                                                                                                |
| `reps`           | `int`       | Runs for each subject in this case, in place of `--reps`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `model`          | `text`      | The model of the agent in this case, in place of `--model`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `judgeModel`     | `text`      | The model that scores the judged checks of this case, in place of `--judge-model`.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `env`            | `envvars`   | Variables the agent's process gets, with the values given here. A name starts with `CASE_`, or is `TZ`, `LANG` or `LC_ALL`.                                                                                                                                                      |
| `minDelta`       | `signed`    | The least score difference, B minus A, that the case must show. A number from -1 to 1; a negative number lets B score lower by at most that much.                                                                                                                                |
| `setup`          | `steps`     | A non-empty list of steps that run in the workspace, in order, before the agent starts: `{ "run": "<shell text>", "timeoutSeconds": 60 }` or `{ "git": { "init": true, "branch": "main", "commitAll": "<message>", "remote": "origin" } }`. A failed step makes the run invalid. |
| `home`           | `text`      | A directory of the case, copied into the run's throwaway home after the login files. It may not hold a file at the path of a harness's login file.                                                                                                                               |
| `fixtures`       | `texts`     | Directories, relative to the case's directory and inside the cases directory, copied into the workspace in order before the case's own `workspace/`. Keep shared ones under a directory that starts with `_`.                                                                    |
| `variants`       | `variants`  | A non-empty list of variants: the same case put differently, such as a paraphrase or a pressure. Each runs as `<case id>@<variant id>`, and the case never runs bare. See the variant keys below.                                                                                |

## Variant keys

The keys of an object in the `variants` list. A variant needs `id` and exactly one of `prompt` and `promptAppend`. Any other key is a load error, except a key that starts with `x-`. See [Organise a suite](../guides/organise-a-suite.md#variants).

| Key            | Type   | Holds                                                                                                                 |
| -------------- | ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`           | `slug` | The variant's name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, unique within the case. The case runs as `<case id>@<id>`. |
| `prompt`       | `text` | The whole prompt of the variant, in place of `prompt.md`. Give this or `promptAppend`, not both.                      |
| `promptAppend` | `text` | Text added to the case's `prompt.md` after a blank line. Needs a `prompt.md`. Give this or `prompt`, not both.        |
| `heldout`      | `bool` | True for a variant that runs only with `--heldout`, so that tuning a skill does not see it. Default: false.           |
| `tags`         | `tags` | Tags added to the case's tags for this variant.                                                                       |

## Tool kinds

A `kind` is one of these words.

| Kind       | Meaning                                                              |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shell`    | Ran a command.                                                       |
| `read`     | Read a file.                                                         |
| `write`    | Created or replaced a file.                                          |
| `edit`     | Changed part of a file, or deleted one.                              |
| `search`   | Searched or listed files.                                            |
| `web`      | Fetched a page or searched the web.                                  |
| `skill`    | Called the harness's skill tool.                                     |
| `subagent` | Started another agent.                                               |
| `other`    | Any tool the harness's adapter has no kind for, such as an MCP tool. |
